title.zh: 卷27 志第22 百官中
title.raw: 卷27 志第22 百官中 Volume 27 Treatises 22: Government Offices 2

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 後齊制官，多循後魏，置太師、太傅、太保，是為三師，擬古上公，非勳德崇者不居。

translations.literal: The Northern Qi system of offices largely followed the Later Wei, establishing Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Protector—these were the Three Preceptors, modeled on the ancient chief dignitaries; none but those of eminent merit and virtue held these posts.
translations.idiomatic: In its system of offices, Northern Qi largely followed Later Wei practice, establishing the Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Protector—the Three Preceptors—modeled on the ancient chief dignitaries. Only men of eminent merit and virtue were appointed to these posts.

sentences.zh: 次有大司馬、大將軍，是為二大，並典司武事。

translations.literal: Next were the Grand Marshal and Grand General—these were the Two Grand ones—both entrusted with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the Grand Marshal and Grand General—the Two Grand ones—both entrusted with military affairs.

sentences.zh: 次置太尉、司徒、司空，是為三公。

translations.literal: Next were established Grand Commandant, Minister over the Masses, and Minister of Works—these were the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Next were established the Grand Commandant, Minister over the Masses, and Minister of Works—the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 三師、二大、三公府三門，當中開黃閤，設內屏，各置長史、司馬、諮議參軍、從事中郎、掾、屬；

translations.literal: The offices of the Three Preceptors, Two Grand ones, and Three Dukes each had three gates, with the Yellow Gate opened in the center and an inner screen set up; each office had a Chief Clerk, Marshal, Advisory Aide-de-Camp, Attendant Gentleman, Clerks, and Assistants;
translations.idiomatic: The offices of the Three Preceptors, Two Grand ones, and Three Dukes each had three gates, with the central Yellow Gate and an inner screen; each office appointed a Chief Clerk, Marshal, Advisory Aide-de-Camp, Attendant Gentleman, clerks, and assistants;

sentences.zh: 主簿、錄事、功曹、記室、戶曹、金曹、中兵、外兵、騎兵、長流、城局、刑獄等參軍事；

translations.literal: Chief Secretary, Recorder, Merit Officer, Secretariat, Household Officer, Finance Officer, Central Military, External Military, Cavalry, Long Flow, City Bureau, Punishments and Prisons, and other Aides-de-Camp for administrative affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Chief Secretary, Recorder, Merit Officer, Secretariat, Household Officer, Finance Officer, Central Military, External Military, Cavalry, Long Flow, City Bureau, Punishments and Prisons, and other aides-de-camp for administrative affairs;

translations.literal: Libationers of the Eastern and Western Pavilions and Aides-de-Camp for administrative affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Libationers of the Eastern and Western Pavilions and aides-de-camp for administrative affairs;

sentences.zh: 法、墨、田、水、鎧、集、士等曹行參軍；

translations.literal: Law, Ink, Field, Water, Armor, Collection, Scholar, and other bureau Acting Aides-de-Camp;
translations.idiomatic: Acting aides-de-camp for the Law, Ink, Field, Water, Armor, Collection, Scholar, and other bureaus;

sentences.zh: 兼左戶、右戶行參軍、長兼行參軍；

translations.literal: Concurrent Left Household and Right Household Acting Aides-de-Camp, and Chief Concurrent Acting Aides-de-Camp;
translations.idiomatic: Concurrent Left Household and Right Household acting aides-de-camp, and chief concurrent acting aides-de-camp;

translations.literal: Aides-de-Camp, Supervisors, and other such posts.
translations.idiomatic: Aides-de-camp, supervisors, and other such posts.

translations.literal: The Minister over the Masses additionally had Left and Right Chief Clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister over the Masses additionally had Left and Right Chief Clerks.

translations.literal: Below the Three Dukes came those of Equal Prestige to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Below the Three Dukes came those of Equal Prestige to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 加開府者，亦置長史已下官屬，而減記室、倉、城局、田、水、鎧、士等七曹，各一人。

translations.literal: Those granted the privilege of opening an office also had Chief Clerks and subordinate officials, but the Secretariat, Granary, City Bureau, Field, Water, Armor, and Scholar bureaus were each reduced by one person.
translations.idiomatic: Those granted the privilege of opening an office also appointed Chief Clerks and subordinate officials, but the Secretariat, Granary, City Bureau, Field, Water, Armor, and Scholar bureaus were each reduced by one person.

sentences.zh: 其品亦每官下三府一階。

translations.literal: Their ranks were also one grade lower than those of the Three Dukes' offices for each post.
translations.idiomatic: Their ranks were also one grade lower than the corresponding posts in the Three Dukes' offices.

sentences.zh: 三師、二大置佐史，則同太尉府。

translations.literal: When the Three Preceptors and Two Grand ones established Assistant Clerks, these were the same as in the Grand Commandant's office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Preceptors and Two Grand ones appointed Assistant Clerks, these were the same as in the Grand Commandant's office.

translations.literal: In the Qianming era, the Chancellor was also established.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianming era, the Chancellor was also established.

sentences.zh: 河清中，分為左右，亦各置府僚云。

translations.literal: In the Heqing era, it was divided into Left and Right, and each also had its own office staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the Heqing era, it was divided into Left and Right, and each also had its own office staff.

sentences.zh: 特進，左、右光祿、金紫、銀青等光祿大夫，用人俱以舊德就閑者居之。

translations.literal: Special Advancement, Left and Right Supervisors of the Palace, Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon Grand Masters of the Palace—all these posts were filled by men of long-standing virtue who had taken retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Special Advancement, Left and Right Supervisors of the Palace, and Grand Masters of the Palace with golden seal and purple ribbon or silver seal and blue ribbon—all these posts were filled by men of long-standing virtue who had retired to honorary positions.

sentences.zh: 自一品已下，從九品已上，又有驃騎、車騎、衛、四征、四鎮、中軍、鎮軍、撫軍、翊軍、四安、冠軍、輔國、龍驤、鎮遠、安遠、建忠、建節、中堅、中壘、振威、奮威、廣德、弘義、折沖、制勝、伏波、陵江、輕車、樓船、勁武、昭勇、明威、顯信、度遼、橫海、逾岷、越嶂、戎昭、武毅、雄烈、恢猛、揚麾、曜鋒、蕩邊，開城、靜漠、綏戎、平越、殄夷、飛騎、隼擊、武牙、武奮、清野、橫野、偏、裨等將軍，以褒賞勳庸。

translations.literal: From the first rank down to the ninth subordinate rank and above, there were also the Flying Cavalry, Chariot and Cavalry, Guard, Four Campaign, Four Pacification, Central Army, Army Pacifier, Army Pacifier, Assisting Army, Four Tranquility, Champion, State Supporter, Dragon Charger, Distant Pacifier, Distant Pacifier, Loyalty Builder, Standard Bearer, Central Firm, Central Rampart, Shaking Might, Exerting Might, Broad Virtue, Expanding Righteousness, Breaking the Foe, Achieving Victory, Subduing the Waves, Crossing the River, Light Chariot, Tower Ship, Vigorous Warrior, Manifest Courage, Bright Might, Displaying Trust, Crossing the Liao, Crossing the Sea, Crossing Min, Crossing the Ridges, Military Manifestation, Martial Resolution, Heroic Fierceness, Restoring Fierceness, Raising the Banner, Shining Edge, Clearing the Border, Opening the City, Quieting the Desert, Pacifying the Barbarians, Pacifying the Yue, Exterminating the Barbarians, Flying Cavalry, Falcon Strike, Martial Fang, Martial Exertion, Clearing the Wilds, Sweeping the Wilds, Lieutenant, and Assistant Generals, to reward meritorious service.
translations.idiomatic: From the first rank down through the ninth subordinate rank, there were also the Flying Cavalry, Chariot and Cavalry, Guard, Four Campaign, Four Pacification, Central Army, Army Pacifier, Army Supporter, Assisting Army, Four Tranquility, Champion, State Supporter, Dragon Charger, Distant Pacifier, Loyalty Builder, Standard Bearer, Central Firm, Central Rampart, Shaking Might, Exerting Might, Broad Virtue, Expanding Righteousness, Breaking the Foe, Achieving Victory, Subduing the Waves, Crossing the River, Light Chariot, Tower Ship, Vigorous Warrior, Manifest Courage, Bright Might, Displaying Trust, Crossing the Liao, Crossing the Sea, Crossing Min, Crossing the Ridges, Military Manifestation, Martial Resolution, Heroic Fierceness, Restoring Fierceness, Raising the Banner, Shining Edge, Clearing the Border, Opening the City, Quieting the Desert, Pacifying the Barbarians, Pacifying the Yue, Exterminating the Barbarians, Flying Cavalry, Falcon Strike, Martial Fang, Martial Exertion, Clearing the Wilds, Sweeping the Wilds, Lieutenant, and Assistant Generals, to reward meritorious service.

sentences.zh: 尚書省，置令，僕射，吏部、殿中、祠部、五兵、都官、度支等六尚書。

translations.literal: The Department of State Affairs had a Director, Vice Directors, and six Ministers: Personnel, Palace Affairs, Sacrificial Affairs, Five Armies, Judicial Affairs, and Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The Department of State Affairs had a Director, Vice Directors, and six Ministers—for Personnel, Palace Affairs, Sacrificial Affairs, Five Armies, Judicial Affairs, and Revenue.

sentences.zh: 又有錄尚書一人，位在令上，掌與令同，但不糾察。

translations.literal: There was also one Recording Director, whose position was above the Director; his authority was the same as the Director's, but he did not conduct inspections.
translations.idiomatic: There was also one Recording Director, whose position ranked above the Director; his authority was the same as the Director's, but he did not conduct inspections.

sentences.zh: 令則彈糾見事，與御史中丞更相廉察。

translations.literal: The Director inspected and corrected current affairs, mutually overseeing one another with the Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The Director inspected and corrected current affairs, mutually overseeing one another with the Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 僕射職為執法，置二則為左、右僕射，皆與令同。

translations.literal: The Vice Director's duty was law enforcement; when two were appointed, they were the Left and Right Vice Directors, both with the same authority as the Director.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Director's duty was law enforcement; when two were appointed, they became the Left and Right Vice Directors, both with the same authority as the Director.

translations.literal: The Left inspected and impeached, while the Right did not inspect and impeach.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Vice Director inspected and impeached, while the Right did not.

sentences.zh: 錄、令、僕射，總理六尚書事，謂之都省。

translations.literal: The Recording Director, Director, and Vice Directors collectively managed the affairs of the six Ministers—this was called the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The Recording Director, Director, and Vice Directors collectively managed the affairs of the six Ministers—this was called the Central Secretariat.

translations.literal: Its subordinate officials:
translations.idiomatic: Its subordinate officials:

sentences.zh: 左丞、掌吏部、考功、主爵、殿中、儀曹、三公、祠部、主客、左右中兵、左右外兵、都官、二千石、度支、左右戶十七曹，並彈糾見事；

translations.literal: The Left Assistant Director oversaw the Personnel, Merit Evaluation, Enfeoffment, Palace Affairs, Ritual, Three Dukes, Sacrificial Affairs, Guest Reception, Left and Right Central Military, Left and Right External Military, Judicial Affairs, Two-Thousand-Bushel, Revenue, and Left and Right Household bureaus—seventeen bureaus in all—and inspected and corrected current affairs;
translations.idiomatic: The Left Assistant Director oversaw seventeen bureaus—Personnel, Merit Evaluation, Enfeoffment, Palace Affairs, Ritual, Three Dukes, Sacrificial Affairs, Guest Reception, Left and Right Central Military, Left and Right External Military, Judicial Affairs, Two-Thousand-Bushel, Revenue, and Left and Right Household—and inspected and corrected current affairs;

sentences.zh: 又主管轄台中，有違失者，兼糾駁之；

translations.literal: He also supervised and had jurisdiction over the inner offices; when there were violations or errors, he also inspected and rebuked them;
translations.idiomatic: He also supervised the inner offices; when violations or errors occurred, he inspected and rebuked them as well;

translations.literal: The Right Assistant Director, one person.
translations.idiomatic: There was one Right Assistant Director.

sentences.zh: 掌駕部、虞曹、屯田、起部、都兵、比部、水部、膳部、倉部、金部、庫部十一曹；

translations.literal: He oversaw the Imperial Carriages, Parks, Colonization, Construction, Central Military, Comparison, Waterways, Provisions, Granaries, Finance, and Armory bureaus—eleven bureaus;
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw eleven bureaus—Imperial Carriages, Parks, Colonization, Construction, Central Military, Comparison, Waterways, Provisions, Granaries, Finance, and Armory;

sentences.zh: 亦管轄台中，又主凡諸用度雜物、脂、燈、筆、墨、幃帳；

translations.literal: He also had jurisdiction over the inner offices, and was in charge of all miscellaneous supplies for use—grease, lamps, brushes, ink, curtains, and tents;
translations.idiomatic: He also had jurisdiction over the inner offices and was in charge of all miscellaneous supplies—grease, lamps, brushes, ink, curtains, and tents;

translations.literal: Only he did not inspect and impeach; in all other respects his duties were the same as the Left.
translations.idiomatic: Only he did not inspect and impeach; in all other respects his duties were the same as the Left Assistant Director's.

sentences.zh: 並都令史八人，共掌其事。

translations.literal: Together with eight Central Secretariat Clerks, they jointly managed these affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Together with eight Central Secretariat Clerks, they jointly managed these affairs.

translations.literal: The six Ministers each supervised various bureaus:
translations.idiomatic: The six Ministers each supervised various bureaus:

sentences.zh: 吏部統：吏部：掌褒崇、選補等事。

translations.literal: Personnel supervised: Personnel: in charge of honors, selection, and appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel supervised: the Personnel Bureau, in charge of honors, selection, and appointment.

sentences.zh: 考功：掌考第及秀孝貢士等事。

translations.literal: Merit Evaluation: in charge of ranking examinations and the presentation of worthy and filial candidates.
translations.idiomatic: Merit Evaluation: in charge of ranking examinations and the presentation of worthy and filial candidates.

translations.literal: Enfeoffment: in charge of granting titles and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffment: in charge of granting titles and ranks.

translations.literal: Three bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Three bureaus.

sentences.zh: 殿中統：殿中：掌駕行百官留守名帳，宮殿禁衛，供御衣倉等事。

translations.literal: Palace Affairs supervised: Palace Affairs: in charge of registers of officials left behind during imperial processions, palace guard duty, and the imperial clothing storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Affairs supervised: the Palace Affairs Bureau, in charge of registers of officials left behind during imperial processions, palace guard duty, and the imperial clothing storehouse.

translations.literal: Ritual: in charge of auspicious and inauspicious ritual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual: in charge of auspicious and inauspicious ritual regulations.

sentences.zh: 三公：掌五時讀時令，諸曹囚帳，斷罪，赦日建金雞等事。

translations.literal: Three Dukes: in charge of reading seasonal ordinances at the five seasons, registers of prisoners in various bureaus, sentencing, and erecting the golden rooster on amnesty days.
translations.idiomatic: Three Dukes: in charge of reading seasonal ordinances at the five seasons, registers of prisoners in various bureaus, sentencing, and erecting the golden rooster on amnesty days.

sentences.zh: 駕部：掌車輿、牛馬廄牧等事。

translations.literal: Imperial Carriages: in charge of chariots and carriages, stables, and livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Carriages: in charge of chariots and carriages, stables, and livestock.

translations.literal: Four bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Four bureaus.

sentences.zh: 祠部統：祠部：掌祠部醫藥，死喪贈賜等事。

translations.literal: Sacrificial Affairs supervised: Sacrificial Affairs: in charge of sacrificial medicine, death and mourning gifts and grants.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial Affairs supervised: the Sacrificial Affairs Bureau, in charge of sacrificial medicine, death and mourning gifts and grants.

translations.literal: Guest Reception: in charge of various foreign guests and tributary envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Guest Reception: in charge of various foreign guests and tributary envoys.

sentences.zh: 虞曹：掌地圖，山川遠近，園囿田獵，肴膳雜味等事。

translations.literal: Parks: in charge of maps, the distances of mountains and rivers, gardens and hunting grounds, and various delicacies for banquets.
translations.idiomatic: Parks: in charge of maps, the distances of mountains and rivers, gardens and hunting grounds, and various delicacies for banquets.

sentences.zh: 屯田：掌藉田、諸州屯田等事。

translations.literal: Colonization: in charge of ceremonial plowing fields and colonization farms in the various provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Colonization: in charge of ceremonial plowing fields and colonization farms in the various provinces.

translations.literal: Construction: in charge of various building projects and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Construction: in charge of various building projects and the like.

translations.literal: Five bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Five bureaus.

sentences.zh: 祠部無尚書則右僕射攝。

translations.literal: When there was no Minister of Sacrificial Affairs, the Right Vice Director acted in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: When there was no Minister of Sacrificial Affairs, the Right Vice Director acted in his stead.

sentences.zh: 五兵統：左中兵：掌諸郡督告身、諸宿衛官等事。

translations.literal: Five Armies supervised: Left Central Military: in charge of appointment credentials for commandery supervisors and palace guard officials.
translations.idiomatic: Five Armies supervised: Left Central Military, in charge of appointment credentials for commandery supervisors and palace guard officials.

sentences.zh: 右中兵：掌畿內丁帳、事力、蕃兵等事。

translations.literal: Right Central Military: in charge of conscription registers within the capital region, corvée labor, and frontier troops.
translations.idiomatic: Right Central Military: in charge of conscription registers within the capital region, corvée labor, and frontier troops.

sentences.zh: 左外兵：掌河南及潼關已東諸州丁帳，及發召徵兵等事。

translations.literal: Left External Military: in charge of conscription registers in Henan and the provinces east of Tong Pass, and mobilizing and conscripting troops.
translations.idiomatic: Left External Military: in charge of conscription registers in Henan and the provinces east of Tong Pass, and mobilizing and conscripting troops.

sentences.zh: 右外兵：掌河北及潼關已西諸州，所典與左外同。

translations.literal: Right External Military: in charge of Hebei and the provinces west of Tong Pass; its duties were the same as the Left External Military.
translations.idiomatic: Right External Military: in charge of Hebei and the provinces west of Tong Pass; its duties were the same as the Left External Military.

sentences.zh: 都兵：掌鼓吹、太樂、雜戶等事。

translations.literal: Central Military: in charge of ceremonial music, the Imperial Music Office, and miscellaneous households.
translations.idiomatic: Central Military: in charge of ceremonial music, the Imperial Music Office, and miscellaneous households.

translations.literal: Five bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Five bureaus.

sentences.zh: 都官統：都官：掌畿內非違得失事。

translations.literal: Judicial Affairs supervised: Judicial Affairs: in charge of violations and merits and demerits within the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Judicial Affairs supervised: the Judicial Affairs Bureau, in charge of violations and merits and demerits within the capital region.

sentences.zh: 二千石：掌畿外得失等事。

translations.literal: Two-Thousand-Bushel: in charge of merits and demerits outside the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Two-Thousand-Bushel: in charge of merits and demerits outside the capital region.

sentences.zh: 比部：掌詔書律令勾檢等事。

translations.literal: Comparison: in charge of verifying imperial edicts, statutes, and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Comparison: in charge of verifying imperial edicts, statutes, and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 水部：掌舟船、津梁，公私水事。

translations.literal: Waterways: in charge of boats and ships, ferries and bridges, and public and private water affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Waterways: in charge of boats and ships, ferries and bridges, and public and private water affairs.

sentences.zh: 膳部：掌侍官百司禮食肴饌等事。

translations.literal: Provisions: in charge of ceremonial meals and delicacies for attending officials and the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: Provisions: in charge of ceremonial meals and delicacies for attending officials and the hundred offices.

translations.literal: Five bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Five bureaus.

sentences.zh: 度支統：度支：掌計會，凡軍國損益、事役糧廩等事。

translations.literal: Revenue supervised: Revenue: in charge of accounting, and all military and state revenues and expenditures, corvée service, and grain stores.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue supervised: the Revenue Bureau, in charge of accounting and all military and state revenues and expenditures, corvée service, and grain stores.

sentences.zh: 倉部：掌諸倉帳出入等事。

translations.literal: Granaries: in charge of registers of receipts and disbursements from the various granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Granaries: in charge of registers of receipts and disbursements from the various granaries.

sentences.zh: 左戶：掌天下計帳、戶籍等事。

translations.literal: Left Household: in charge of tax registers and household registers throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Left Household: in charge of tax registers and household registers throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 右戶：掌天下公私田宅租調等事。

translations.literal: Right Household: in charge of land and property taxes and corvée levies on public and private fields and dwellings throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Right Household: in charge of land and property taxes and corvée levies on public and private fields and dwellings throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 金部：掌權衡量度、外內諸庫藏文帳等事。

translations.literal: Finance: in charge of weights and measures, and written registers of the various internal and external storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: Finance: in charge of weights and measures, and written registers of the various internal and external storehouses.

sentences.zh: 庫部：掌凡是戎仗器用所須事。

translations.literal: Armory: in charge of all military equipment and implements required for use.
translations.idiomatic: Armory: in charge of all military equipment and implements required for use.

translations.literal: Six bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Six bureaus.

translations.literal: Twenty-eight bureaus in all.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-eight bureaus in all.

sentences.zh: 吏部、三公，郎中各二人，餘並一人。

translations.literal: Personnel and Three Dukes each had two Senior Clerks; all the rest had one each.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel and Three Dukes each had two Senior Clerks; all the rest had one each.

translations.literal: Thirty Senior Clerks in all.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty Senior Clerks in all.

sentences.zh: 吏部、儀曹、三公、虞曹、都官、二千石、比部、左戶、各量事置掌故、主事員。

translations.literal: Personnel, Ritual, Three Dukes, Parks, Judicial Affairs, Two-Thousand-Bushel, Comparison, and Left Household each had Record Keepers and Administrative Clerks appointed according to the volume of business.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel, Ritual, Three Dukes, Parks, Judicial Affairs, Two-Thousand-Bushel, Comparison, and Left Household each had Record Keepers and Administrative Clerks appointed according to the volume of business.

sentences.zh: 門下省，掌獻納諫正，及司進御之職。

translations.literal: The Chancellery was in charge of presenting remonstrances and corrections, and overseeing the service of the imperial household.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellery was in charge of presenting remonstrances and corrections, and overseeing the service of the imperial household.

sentences.zh: 侍中、給事黃門侍郎各六人，錄事四人，通事令史、主事令史八人。

translations.literal: Attendants-in-Ordinary and Supervising Secretaries of the Yellow Gate, six each; Recorders, four; General Affairs Clerks and Administrative Clerks, eight.
translations.idiomatic: There were six Attendants-in-Ordinary and six Supervising Secretaries of the Yellow Gate, four Recorders, and eight General Affairs Clerks and Administrative Clerks.

translations.literal: It supervised six bureaus:
translations.idiomatic: It supervised six bureaus:

sentences.zh: 領左右局，領左右各二人，掌知硃華閣內諸事，宣傳已下，白衣齋子已上，皆主之。

translations.literal: The Left and Right Attendants Bureau had two Left and Right Attendants each, in charge of all affairs within the Vermilion Flower Pavilion; from heralds down to white-robed attendants and above, all were under their authority.
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Attendants Bureau had two Left and Right Attendants each, in charge of all affairs within the Vermilion Flower Pavilion; from heralds down to white-robed attendants and above, all were under their authority.

translations.literal: Left and Right Direct Chiefs, four persons.
translations.idiomatic: There were four Left and Right Direct Chiefs.

sentences.zh: 尚食局，典御二人，總知御膳事。

translations.literal: The Imperial Food Bureau had two Palace Stewards who collectively oversaw imperial meals.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Food Bureau had two Palace Stewards who collectively oversaw imperial meals.

translations.literal: Assistants and Supervisors, four each.
translations.idiomatic: There were four Assistants and four Supervisors.

sentences.zh: 尚藥局，典御及丞各二人，總知御藥事。

translations.literal: The Imperial Pharmacy Bureau had two Palace Stewards and two Assistants who collectively oversaw imperial medicine.

translations.literal: The Three Dukes held nine grades of appointment, the Three Solitaries eight, the Six Ministers seven, Upper Grand Masters six, Middle Grand Masters five, Lower Grand Masters four, Upper Gentlemen three, Middle Gentlemen two grades, and Lower Gentlemen one.

sentences.zh: 諸公九命，諸侯八命，諸伯七命，諸子六命，諸男五命，諸公之孤卿四命，侯之孤卿、公之大夫三命，子男之孤卿、侯伯之大夫、公之上士再命，子男之大夫、公之中士、侯伯之上士一命，公之下士、侯伯之中士下士、子男之士不命。

translations.literal: Feudal dukes held nine grades, marquises eight, earls seven, viscounts six, barons five; the Solitary Ministers and Directors of feudal dukes four; the Solitary Ministers and Directors of marquises three; the Solitary Ministers and Directors of viscounts and barons, the Grand Masters of marquises and earls, and the Upper Gentlemen of dukes two; the Grand Masters of viscounts and barons, the Middle Gentlemen of dukes, and the Upper Gentlemen of marquises and earls one; the Lower Gentlemen of dukes, the Middle and Lower Gentlemen of marquises and earls, and the Gentlemen of viscounts and barons received no grade of appointment.

sentences.zh: 其制祿秩，下士一百二十五石，中士已上，至於上大夫，各倍之。

translations.literal: For salary grades, Lower Gentlemen received one hundred twenty-five shi; from Middle Gentlemen upward to Upper Grand Masters, each rank doubled the previous.
translations.idiomatic: For salary grades, Lower Gentlemen received one hundred twenty-five shi; from Middle Gentlemen upward to Upper Grand Masters, each rank doubled the previous.

translations.literal: Upper Grand Masters thus received four thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: Upper Grand Masters thus received four thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 卿二分，孤三分，公四分，各益其一。

translations.literal: Ministers received two shares, Solitary Ministers three, and Dukes four, each adding one share.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers received two shares, Solitary Ministers three, and Dukes four, each adding one share.

translations.literal: Dukes, by the full number, received ten thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes, by the full number, received ten thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 其九秩一百二十石，八秩至於七秩，每二秩六分而下各去其一，二秩一秩俱為四十石。

translations.literal: The ninth grade was one hundred twenty shi; from the eighth through the seventh grade, each two grades reduced by one-sixth; the second and first grades were both forty shi.
translations.idiomatic: The ninth grade was one hundred twenty shi; from the eighth through the seventh grade, each two grades reduced by one-sixth; the second and first grades were both forty shi.

translations.idiomatic: Salaries were distributed according to the quality of the year's harvest.

translations.idiomatic: When the yield reached four fu per mu, it was a good year, and the full salary was distributed.

sentences.zh: 三釜為中年，中年頒其半。

translations.literal: Three fu was an average year, and half the salary was distributed.
translations.idiomatic: Three fu was an average year, and half the salary was distributed.

sentences.zh: 二釜為下年，下年頒其一。

translations.literal: Two fu was a poor year, and one-third of the salary was distributed.
translations.idiomatic: Two fu was a poor year, and one-third of the salary was distributed.

translations.literal: When there was no harvest, it was a year of famine and disaster, and no salary was distributed.
translations.idiomatic: When there was no harvest, it was a year of famine and disaster, and no salary was distributed.
